analyst_view.overall: Inter Escaldes, the first Andorran side in a league phase, are 35th with no points, while Copenhagen are 6th with 7 points and unbeaten in Europe, chasing a top-eight place. Copenhagen come off a 5-0 league defeat at Nordsjaelland, and the club's squad list confirms first-choice keeper Diant Ramaj is injured, so Runar Alex Runarsson should start; Mattsson, Nasnas and Ramaj are listed as injured, Andreas Cornelius and Asger Sorensen stayed in Copenhagen, while Maseko (counted as out) and Markgraf, whose red card was a league ban only, travel. Inter are without Domi Berlanga and, according to two previews, defender Alex Sanchez through suspension. Copenhagen host Midtjylland on Sunday and have rotated a lot lately, and the game is at altitude in Encamp after a long trip. Maltese referee Matthew De Gabriele has no usable record in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already cut for Maseko's absence (-6% on Copenhagen's goals), though he is in the travelling squad. I lean slightly higher, to about 3.0: Ramaj is now confirmed out, so backup Runarsson starts behind a defence that just shipped five, and Inter lose defender Alex Sanchez to a ban on top of Berlanga, neither of which the numbers know. Cornelius staying home and likely rotation before Midtjylland keep the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, split almost evenly. Copenhagen should have most of the ball against one of the weakest sides in the competition, but their recent corner count is already trimmed by momentum and a rotated side before Midtjylland may be less sharp, so the two cancel out and I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already counting both sides' recent card counts. Inter have two players suspended for yellow-card build-up, which shows how often they end up chasing games, but that is in their record; Markgraf's red brings only a league ban and referee De Gabriele has no record here that points either way, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.4 shots, already cut for Inter's low shot count lately (-8%). Copenhagen have kept only about half their side from game to game recently and play Midtjylland on Sunday, and the altitude may slow the pace, but there is no lineup news to say how much, so I stay at 23.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, with Inter's few efforts on target (-6%) and Copenhagen's chances against a leaky defence (+3%) already counted. A backup goalkeeper changes how many go in more than how many are on target, so I stay at 9.1.
